title: Starter: networks & the shell
description: A sample module bundling two built-in lessons. Import it to try modules.
author: visilearn

scenes.source:
scene net.ports "Ports: doors on a server"
about "One server can run many services. Each one listens on its own port number."
use net

host you 10.0.0.5 label="You"
server srv 10.0.0.80 port=80,443,22 label="Server"

link you srv

step "Each service has a door number"
  note srv "Listening: 80 (HTTP), 443 (HTTPS), 22 (SSH)"
  you send srv:80
  you send srv:443

step "Knocking on a closed door"
  ask "Nothing listens on port 3306 (MySQL). What will the server do?" "Accept it anyway" "Refuse the connection" "Forward it" answer=2
  you send srv:3306

step "Quick check"
  ask "Which port does HTTPS use by default?" 22|80|443 answer=443
  ask "Which port does SSH use by default?" 21|22|23 answer=22

scene linux.navigate "Finding your way around"
about "The Linux filesystem is one big tree. pwd tells you where you are, ls looks around, cd moves."
use linux

fs as=asha
  home/
    asha/
      notes.txt "buy milk"
      projects/
        app.py "print('hello')"
        README.md "My first app"
  etc/
    hosts "127.0.0.1 localhost"
  tmp/

step "Everything starts at /"
  say "Linux keeps every file in a single tree. The very top is called root and is written as /."
  highlight /
  note / "root: the top of the tree"

step "Where am I?"
  say "Your terminal is always inside one folder. pwd (print working directory) shows its full path."
  run pwd
  note /home/asha "your home folder"

step "Look around"
  ask "What will ls show right now?" "Every file on the computer" "What is inside /home/asha" "Only files, never folders" answer=2
  run ls

step "Move with cd"
  run "cd projects"
  run ls
  say "Watch the badge move. projects is a relative path; /home/asha/projects is the absolute path to the same place."

step "Go back up"
  ask "Which command goes up one level, back to /home/asha?" "cd .." "cd /" "cd up" answer=1
  run "cd .."

step "Your turn"
  say "Use the terminal below: go to /etc and print the hosts file."
  hint "cd /etc   then   cat hosts"
  goal cwd /etc, ran cat, output "localhost"
